basic_info: 48-year-old female presenting with right elbow pain following a popping sensation while lifting a box during moving.
present_illness: Right elbow pain began yesterday following a popping sensation while lifting a box during moving. The pain is described as throbbing. The pain worsens when ice is removed, and there is swelling and redness around the elbow. The patient experiences pain when bending or straightening the arm. No locking, clicking, or instability has been reported.
past_history: No prior elbow injuries, surgeries, or conditions reported. The patient has a history of neck surgery but no history of arthritis or tendinitis in the elbow. No previous episodes of similar elbow pain or injury reported.
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, Temp 36.8°C. Physical examination of the right elbow reveals localized swelling and redness without bruising. There is tenderness over the lateral epicondyle. Range of motion is limited due to pain, with no deformity noted. Neurological examination shows intact sensation and motor function in the arm and hand. No locking, clicking, or instability noted in the elbow joint.
aux_exam: X-rays of the right elbow were performed and showed no fractures but noted swelling on the lateral side. No further imaging or diagnostic tests have been conducted.
